Winger vs striker vs full-back: what is the difference?

A winger starts wide and creates from the flank, a striker starts central and is the team's main finisher, and a full-back defends the flank first and attacks second. "Forward" is the umbrella word: in a 4-3-3 the two wingers and the striker are all forwards. The difference is where you start and what you are judged on.

PositionStartsMain jobJudged on
WingerWide, near the touchline, front line or wide midfieldStretch the defense, beat the full-back, create and score from wideChances created, goals, 1v1s won, tracking back
Striker (the 9)Central, highest playerScore, hold the ball up, run in behind the center backsGoals, link play, pressing the center backs
Number 10Central, between their midfield and defenseReceive between the lines, play the final passChances created, assists, goals from the edge of the box
Full-backWide in the back lineDefend the opposing winger, overlap or underlap in attack1v1 defending, crosses stopped, support in attack

Wingers and full-backs on the same side work as a pair: when you go inside, he gets the touchline, and when he goes forward, you cover for him. Our guides to the striker and the number 10 cover the central roles.

Set pieces: wingers often take corners and wide free kicks because of their delivery. When you defend a corner, your coach may keep you higher up as the outlet for a counter-attack, or ask you to guard the edge of the box.

Which wingers should you study?

The wingers most worth studying are the ones who show one clear skill very well: Garrincha and Stanley Matthews for 1v1 dribbling, Ryan Giggs for traditional wing play, Arjen Robben for the inverted cut inside, and today Vinícius Júnior and Bukayo Saka. Pick one who plays your side with your strong foot.

PlayerSide and footWhat to study
Garrincha (Brazil)Right wingBeating the full-back on the outside. Won the 1958 and 1962 World Cups with Brazil.
Stanley Matthews (England)Right wingFeints and change of pace in the 1v1. The first Ballon d'Or winner, in 1956.
George Best (Manchester United)Either sideBalance and close control at speed. Won the Ballon d'Or in 1968.
Ryan Giggs (Manchester United)Left wing, left footThe traditional winger: down the line and cross.
Arjen Robben (Bayern Munich, Netherlands)Right wing, left footThe inverted winger's cut inside and curled shot to the far post.
Megan Rapinoe (USA)Left wingCrosses and set-piece delivery. Won the Golden Ball at the 2019 Women's World Cup.
Vinícius Júnior (Real Madrid, Brazil)Left wing, right footChanges of pace in the 1v1 and runs in behind.
Bukayo Saka (Arsenal, England)Right wing, left footReceiving on the half-turn, then choosing inside or outside.

How can I train to be a winger on my own?

Train half-turn receiving against a wall, 1v1 changes of pace with a friend or cones, cutting inside and finishing within two touches, and cut-backs and crosses from the byline. Add decision practice by pausing match footage or using situation tests.
ops.replace:
How can I train to be a winger on my own?

Train half-turn receiving against a wall, 1v1 changes of pace with a friend or cones, cutting inside and finishing within two touches, and cut-backs and crosses from the byline. Add decision practice by pausing match footage or using situation tests.

What is the difference between a winger and a striker?

A striker plays centrally, closest to goal, and his main job is scoring. A winger starts wide near the touchline, stretches the defense, beats full-backs 1v1 and creates chances with crosses and cut-backs. Modern wingers also score a lot by cutting inside or arriving at the back post.

Do you have to be fast to play winger?

Speed helps, but it is not required. Many wingers win their 1v1s with a change of pace, a good first touch and timing rather than top speed. If you are not quick, receive on the half-turn, go at your man early, and use cut-backs and one-twos instead of long foot races.

What does a winger do at corners?

Wingers often take corners because of their delivery. When defending a corner, many teams keep one winger higher up the field as the outlet for a counter-attack, while the other guards the edge of the box or marks a short-corner option. Your coach decides which job is yours.

Who is the best winger of all time?

There is no official answer. Names that come up most are Garrincha, Stanley Matthews, George Best, Ryan Giggs, Arjen Robben and Cristiano Ronaldo, who started as a winger. To learn, pick one who plays your side with your strong foot and study his decisions, not only his highlights.
